Pankaj And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 May,
2023

Author: Rajiv Gupta
Bench: Rajiv Gupta
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:112731
Court No. - 65
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 13580 of 2023
Applicant :- Pankaj And 2 Others

Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Shravan Kumar Singh

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Rajiv Gupta,J.
1.Supplementary affidavit filed today in Court, is taken on record.
2.Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.

3.This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed with a prayer to quash the entire proceedings of Criminal Case No. 2891 of 2023 (State vs. Pankaj and and others) arising out of Case Crime No. 5 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 323 IPC, P.S. Sector-142, Noida, District- Gautam Budh Nagar, pending in the court of Civil Judge (Junior Division)/Fast Track Court, Court No. 1, Gautam Budh Nagar.
Pankaj And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158142217/
1 4.Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted that opposite party No. 2 is the wife of applicant No. 1 and applicant Nos. 2 and 3 are the sister in-law and mother in-law of opposite party No. 2.
Learned counsel for the applicant has next submitted that on account of matrimonial discord, the present criminal case was instituted against the applicants, however, with the intervention of the respected members of both the family and society, they have amicably settled all their disputes and differences and now they do not have any grievance against the each other.

sentences.text: A settlement-agreement dated 28.2.2023 has been drawn between the parties, a copy of which has been annexed as Annexue No. 5 to this application.

5.Learned counsel for the applicants has next submitted that as per the settlement-agreement,
applicant No. 1 and opposite party No. 2 have restored their relationship and are living together as husband and wife and leading a happy married life.

6.This court vide order dated 18.4.2023 had directed the parties to appear before the court below and to file the compromise, which shall be verified in the presence of the parties and after verification, a report shall be submitted by the trial court.

7.Pursuant to the said order, both the parties appeared before the trial court and filed the compromise made between the parties and in their presence, the said compromise has been verified and a report dated 27.4.2023 has been forwarded to this Court, a copy of which has been filed as Annexure- SA-2 to the supplementary affidavit.
8.Learned counsel for the applicants has next submitted that in view of the compromise made between the parties, the entire proceedings be quashed.
9. Learned AGA could not dispute the settlement-agreement made between the parties.

10.This Court is not unmindful of the judgements of the Apex Court in the cases of :-
1. B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and another (2003) 4 SCC 675.
2. Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation [2008) 9 SCC 677].
3. Manoj Sharma Vs. State and others ( 2008) 16 SCC 1.
4. Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 303.
5. Narindra Singh and others Vs. State of Punjab ( 2014) 6 SCC 466.
Wherein the Apex Court has categorically held that compromise can be made between the parties even in respect of certain cognizable and non compoundable offences.

12.Accordingly, Criminal Case No. 2891 of 2023 (State vs. Pankaj and and others) arising out of Case Crime No. 5 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 323 IPC, P.S. Sector-142, Noida, District- Gautam Budh Nagar, pending in the court of Civil Judge (Junior Division)/Fast Track Court, Court No. 1, Gautam Budh Nagar, are hereby quashed.
